summary: Phase A — Notification Incident Recovery independent verification. All 10 review items pass. Ran the main pytest suite (test_phase_a_notifications.py, 9/9) plus a new extended suite (test_phase_a_extended.py, 6/6) that specifically covers the review items not asserted in the main file: unauthenticated /api/register-push, POST /api/inbox/all/read dual-source marking, DELETE /api/broadcasts on unsent broadcast, /api/push/status regression, primary_owner pending_count, and doctor@example.com hygiene. Total 15/15 backend tests green. Frontend /notifications screen renders correctly for both guest ('You're all caught up' empty state) and signed-in (session token injected into localStorage — feed loads from /api/inbox/all with notif-* testIDs). No red screen or console errors. Fixture cleanup verified — 0 TEST_ residue in DB. Item 8 (typed 503) + item 2 (installation_id dedupe) + item 5 (broadcast_inbox mark-read via /api/notifications/{id}/read) + item 7 (primary_owner auto-approver, pending_count, delete unsent) + item 10 (DB hygiene) all pass end-to-end against the live preview URL.
critical_code_review_comments: push_register.py: typed HTTPException detail shape ({error_code, message, mirrored}) is consistent across the three failure branches (relay_not_configured / relay_unauthorized / relay_upstream_error). Client can key off detail.error_code deterministically.

push_register.py: installation_id dedupe is implemented as upsert-by-(user_id,installation_id) + delete_many stale rows carrying same token under a different installation_id — this correctly handles both FCM-token-rotation AND app-reinstall-with-new-install-id scenarios.

broadcasts.py: _is_broadcast_approver() now correctly uses OWNER_TIER_ROLES (primary_owner, partner, super_owner, legacy owner) OR can_approve_broadcasts capability. This closes the legacy `role == 'owner'` string check that was locking primary_owner out after the 4-tier migration.
notifications.py: mark_notification_read now cascades to broadcast_inbox by matching both `inbox_id` and `broadcast_id`. Unknown ids still return 404. Good defensive pattern.

notifications router still lacks a bulk endpoint for JUST broadcast_inbox rows — but /api/broadcasts/inbox/read exists and /api/inbox/all/read does both. Coverage is complete, just spread across three routers. Not a bug.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_phase_a_extended.py (new — 6 additional tests covering review items not in the main suite)

success_rate.frontend: 100% (notifications screen renders both guest + signed-in states, no errors)
